text:
maria.sre: FYI customer (acme-prod) is seeing all inference requests get routed to us-east and higher latency. They say region should be eu-west.
kevin.support: ugh. do we have a repro + sample client IP?
maria.sre: they captured our ingestion logs — source shows 34.198.12.45 which is our hub NAT, not the original client IP. looks like their on-prem proxy is SNATing to the peered hub IP.
liz.ops: that would explain region selection — routing uses source-IP geolocation to pick region variant. if everything SNATs to a US egress we pick us-east.
jamal.eng: can you paste the raw headers from the request? sometimes proxies include X-Forwarded-For but our router code prefers src ip when present.
maria.sre: header dump from their capture:

    GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
    Host: api.redwood.example
    X-Forwarded-For: 81.2.69.23, 34.198.12.45
    X-Real-IP: 81.2.69.23
    User-Agent: acme-ml/1.2.0

kevin.support: interesting — X-Real-IP set correctly but our smart router still picked 34.198.12.45?
jamal.eng: looks like the fronting proxy (customer -> hub -> us-east) is reassigning source at TCP layer; our UDP/geo mapping service queries the TCP connection src ip, not XFF. we do have a header override feature but it's off for private/VPC by default for security.
liz.ops: customer is on a peered hub VPC with central NAT. common onprem pattern: hairpin NAT from their proxy to hub then back out, SNATing to hub IP.
kevin.support: asked customer for quick repro steps. they sent this:

    # from their on-prem proxy host
    curl -v -H "X-Forwarded-For: 81.2.69.23" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -o /tmp/out.log

    tcpdump -nni eth0 host api.redwood.example -w capture.pcap

kevin.support: capture shows TCP src = 34.198.12.45 on the wire to our edge. so XFF is not trusted or overwritten by intermediate layer.
maria.sre: customer asked if we can honor X-Real-IP/X-Forwarded-For from their proxy. they're locked down and can't change the hub NAT.
jamal.eng: options: 1) advise customer to use per-region egress IPs (allocate NAT IPs in eu pool for that spoke) 2) enable our header-trust feature for their account so router uses X-Real-IP/X-Forwarded-For for region selection 3) add a routing exception so traffic from hub IP maps to eu region (manual mapping).
liz.ops: 1 and 3 require changes on their infra (or peering config). 2 is the fastest but has risk if XFF is spoofed; we should gate it to authorized peered CIDRs and only for private deployments.
kevin.support: recommended path to customer: enable proxy to append X-Forwarded-For and also add the hub->redwood connection to a trusted CIDR allowlist. meanwhile we can add a temporary mapping so that traffic from 34.198.12.45 is treated as eu-west for routing.
maria.sre: customer replied: they can't change the hub NAT today, will allow an allowlist change on their side. they want us to apply the mapping now while they test.
jamal.eng: I can add a per-account mapping rule: eg in router config add { "src_ip": "34.198.12.45", "dest_region": "eu-west-1", "note": "temp fix for ACME hub egress" } — will need audit and ops approval.
liz.ops: please include TTL on mapping (48h) and create a ticket for a proper fix (either per-spoke NAT or enable header-trust).
kevin.support: filed internal ticket: INC-6291, assigned to jamal.eng and liz.ops. told customer ETA ~2-4h for mapping. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: router-config changeset 2026-11-03T14:45Z -> reviewers: jamal.eng, liz.ops
maria.sre: thanks team. follow-up notes for runbook: if private/VPC customers use hub/peered NAT, prefer: - per-spoke NAT IPs per-region - or preserve original src IP via proxy (no SNAT) - or explicit header-trust allowlist and validation. also log geo-decisions in trace for faster debug.
kevin.support: adding that to support KB entry: "Egress NAT & wrong-region selection (private/VPC)"
jamal.eng: once mapping is live, I'll post verification steps. simple check: curl with XFF set to client IP and verify we see eu region in connection logs, and latency drops.
maria.sre: verified mapping in staging; customer will test soon. will post results here. :white_check_mark:
